title: Evidence Broker + Retention Simulator for Dedicated Tenant Isolation Assertions
creator: Marina Soto
description: Build a lightweight Evidence Broker component plus a configurable Retention Simulator that jointly produce tenant-level isolation assertions for Dedicated capacity customers. The Evidence Broker will collect deterministic signals (node assignment, geolocation, routing policy, audit logs, KMS key IDs) and transient telemetry (container instance IDs, attested timestamps, ephemeral network endpoints) and assemble signed assertion bundles suitable for compliance review. The Retention Simulator is a deterministic engine that can replay retention policies across a tenant's event stream to validate that data lifecycle settings (delete/expire/migrate) behave as expected before runtime enforcement. Goals: 1) provide tamper-evident assertion bundles for audits, 2) enable pre-deployment validation of retention configurations, 3) surface drift between configured and observed retention behaviors, 4) integrate with Console's evidence export UI and the existing attestation storage bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence Broker can ingest and normalize signals from at least 4 sources: node registry, routing decisions, audit logs, and KMS metadata
Broker produces a signed JSON-LD bundle with a stable schema and Sigstore-compatible signature metadata
Retention Simulator can run a tenant event trace and output a list of items that would be deleted/expired under a given retention policy
Console can request and download an evidence bundle via a new /api/v1/evidence/{tenant_id}?since= endpoint
End-to-end integration test that seeds a synthetic tenant, applies retention policy X, and demonstrates expected deletions in simulator output
Security review completed and threat model updated; any crypto keys or signing services documented
design_notes: Prefer append-only event ingestion from the audit pipeline rather than synchronous calls from serving runtime to avoid latency coupling
Evidence Broker to persist intermediate artifacts in signed, versioned S3 objects with a metadata index in DynamoDB for fast lookups
Use Sigstore-style signatures for bundle authenticity; retention simulator outputs include provenance pointers back to original audit records
Simulator will support policy rules: TTL by object type, user-driven delete, geo-migration holds, and legal-hold exceptions
Design must account for redaction rules: PII fields must be hashed with tenant-specific salts before inclusion in public bundles
api_contracts: POST /internal/broker/ingest - accepts gzipped event batches with X-Redwood-Signature header
GET /api/v1/evidence/{tenant_id}?since= - authenticated Console endpoint to list available bundles
implementation_plan: Week 1: Wire up event adapters for audit-logs and node-registry; schema mapping and example payloads
Week 2: Implement Broker ingest API and a prototype bundle serializer with signature metadata
Week 3: Build Retention Simulator engine and simple policy DSL, unit tests for policy evaluation
Week 4: Console integration endpoints, feature flag behind dedicated-tenant evidence, UX stub for download
Week 5: End-to-end tests, seeding synthetic tenant traces, performance and cost review
Week 6: Security review, finalize signing key rotation plan, documentation and runbook
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Including PII in bundles could violate contracts. Mitigation: enforce redaction + tenant-salt hashing and provide clear opt-in for richer audit exports
Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: use HSM/KMS-backed signing and implement short-lived delegation tokens with automatic rotation
Risk: High ingestion volume from audit pipeline. Mitigation: backpressure via sampling, incremental bundle windows, and consumer-side deduplication
Risk: Simulator divergence from production retention. Mitigation: periodic calibration jobs comparing simulator predictions vs actual deletion metrics; alert on drift beyond threshold
test_plan: Unit tests for schema normalization and redaction rules
Property-based tests for policy DSL to ensure consistent evaluation across inputs
Integration tests: ingest synthetic events -> generate bundle -> validate signature -> Console download
Load test: broker ingest at 10k events/min sustained over 30 minutes; monitor memory and S3 PUT rate
Chaos test: rotate signing key during bundle generation to verify retry and tombstone behavior
